hints: Look at what each cell actually does in the diagram. Which cell (H or G) secretes antibodies, and which cell (G) touches and kills the virus-infected host cell?
Notice cell F sends chemical stimulation to both sides of the diagram. Which type of T cell is the coordinator that stimulates both B cells and killer cells?
walkthrough:
**Start with the easy jobs, H and G**

Look at the bottom of the diagram. Cell H is large and shows secretion of antibodies. Only plasma cells do that, so H must be a plasma cell.

On the right, cell G binds directly to the host cell infected with virus. That is cell-mediated killing, so G must be a T-killer (cytotoxic T) cell.

**Identify the coordinator, F**

Cell F gives chemical stimulation (cytokines) to the left side to help activate B cells and to help form H. T-helper cells are the coordinators that release cytokines to stimulate both B cells and T-killer cells. So F is a T-helper cell.

**Identify the leftover, E**

On the far left, cell E is produced by clonal expansion of the activated B cell but does not secrete antibody. That is the classic role of a B-memory cell, kept in reserve for a faster secondary response. This gives E = B-memory, F = T-helper, G = T-killer, H = plasma, which is row A.

options.A: Perfect match. E is B-memory, F is T-helper giving cytokines, G is T-killer destroying infected cell, H is plasma cell secreting antibody.
options.B: E and H are right, but F cannot be T-memory and G cannot be macrophage. Macrophages phagocytose, they do not kill infected cells by direct contact like G does.
options.C: Back to front. Plasma cells secrete antibody so H not E, and T-helper cells give stimulation so they are F not G.
options.D: All swapped. E is from the B cell line not a T-killer, F is the helper not memory, and H secretes antibody so it is plasma not T-helper.
